ground_truth.mechanism: card_title replaces only a fixed list of '<', '>' and dot look-alikes plus characters in the Ps/Pe/Pi/Pf bracket categories, so a model-written chat title can carry look-alikes outside that list, such as Canadian Syllabics ᐳ/ᐸ (Lo), ᐧ (Lo, a final middle dot), Hangul ㆍ (Lo) or Runic ᛫ (Po). These draw an arrow-bracket or a ' · ' on the approval card's provenance line, which breaks the documented rule that look-alikes become '_'. With the card's one-line ellipsis this can fake the '(Provider · id)' suffix; the effect is display-only.

non_issues.claim: The HUD cardTitle test suite has no case with a decomposed (NFD) title, so dropping the TypeScript NFC normalization would not make any HUD test fail.
non_issues.why_not: The HUD test already has a decomposed (NFD) case. A byte-level match shows line 197 calls cardTitle with "cafe" + U+0301 and expects the precomposed "caf\u00e9". Without the TypeScript normalize("NFC"), CARD_DROPPED (\p{Mn}) would drop U+0301 and return "cafe", so the test would fail. Removing the NFC normalization does break a HUD test.
non_issues.source: pooled cluster p1, ruled invalid, accepted as a non-issue by lead on 2026-10-23

non_issues.claim: When the HUD build output is missing, the face relay check suite skips every check but still exits with status zero, so exit-code gating reports a pass.
non_issues.why_not: The code doesn't do what the claim says. When hud/dist/index.html is missing, main() prints the build hint and returns 2, and the `__main__` guard passes that to sys.exit(main()). The suite therefore exits with status 2, not 0, so a gate that checks the exit code sees a failure rather than a pass.
